Compute Cell-to-Cell Ligand-Receptor Signals

Source: R/compute_CellToCell.R
compute_CellToCell.Rd

Universal scoring engine for all NICHESv2 edge modes. For each edge and each valid LR pair, computes a signal score. The edge list may come from either edgelist constructor – spatial or type-sampled – and the count matrix column names must be the cell barcodes it uses.

Supports multi-gene complexes: a ligand or receptor represented as "gene1_gene2" is split on "_" and all component expressions are combined via the chosen method (product or minimum) across all ligand and receptor components together.

Built-in LRM databases can be loaded by name (see load_LRM_database):

  • "fantom5" – Ramilowski et al. 2015. Bundled with NICHESv2 (human, mouse, rat, pig). No internet or extra packages required.

  • "omnipath" – OmniPath intercell network (Turei et al. 2021). Requires the OmnipathR package and internet access.

Usage

compute_CellToCell(
  count.mtx,
  edge.list,
  LRM.db,
  ligand.col = "ligand",
  receptor.col = "receptor",
  method = c("product", "minimum"),
  n.cores = 1L
)

Arguments

count.mtx

Gene x cell expression matrix (sparse dgCMatrix or dense). Row names = gene symbols; column names = cell barcodes matching edge.list$from / $to.

edge.list

data.table from create_Edgelist_Spatial or create_Edgelist_SamplingByType; or any data.frame with from and to columns whose values match colnames(count.mtx). Coordinate columns (x.from, y.from, x.to, y.to), when present, are propagated to the output.

LRM.db

LR pair table (data.frame or data.table) or a character string ("fantom5" or "omnipath") loaded via load_LRM_database. When a string is passed, ligand.col and receptor.col are silently overridden to the canonical "ligand" and "receptor".

ligand.col

Character. Column name for ligand symbols in LRM.db. Default "ligand". Ignored when LRM.db is a built-in database name.

receptor.col

Character. Column name for receptor symbols in LRM.db. Default "receptor". Ignored when LRM.db is a built-in database name.

method

Per-edge LR scoring method. "product" (default) multiplies sender ligand expression by receiver receptor expression; "minimum" takes the elementwise minimum across all ligand and receptor components. See the Complex scoring section.

n.cores

Integer. CPU cores for parallel LRM-chunk processing. Default 1L. See the Parallelization section.

Value

A plain named list with two elements:

$edges

data.table: from, to, ligand, receptor, LRM ("ligand|receptor"), score. Additional columns x.from, y.from, x.to, y.to appear only when the input edge.list carries coordinates (i.e.\ for spatial edge lists). One row per non-zero (edge x LRM) combination – silent pairs are omitted for sparsity. Keyed on (from, to, LRM).

$lr.meta

data.table: ligand, receptor, LRM, plus any extra annotation columns present in LRM.db (e.g.\ pathway). One row per valid LRM pair after gene-availability filtering. Keyed on (ligand, receptor).

Both elements are data.tables so downstream joins on from/to/LRM are O(log n).

Complex scoring example

LRM "COL1A1_COL1A2 -> ITGB1" with method = "product": $$score = \text{expr}_{send}(COL1A1) \times \text{expr}_{send}(COL1A2) \times \text{expr}_{recv}(ITGB1)$$ With method = "minimum": $$score = \min(\text{expr}_{send}(COL1A1),\ \text{expr}_{send}(COL1A2),\ \text{expr}_{recv}(ITGB1))$$

Direct vs wrapped use

Most users should call create_NICHESObject, which invokes compute_CellToCell() internally and assembles the result into a full NICHESObject. Call this function directly when you only need the raw (edge, LRM, score) table – for example, to score a custom edge list (e.g.\ a CCC graph from another method) without building the surrounding object, or to integrate the score table into a non-NICHESv2 downstream pipeline.

Parallelization

Work is partitioned across LRM pairs into n.cores chunks and processed by a socket cluster (parallel::makeCluster), which works identically on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Each worker has its data.table thread count throttled to 1 to prevent OpenMP contention with the outer parallelism. The cluster is torn down via on.exit(stopCluster(cl)) so it is released even if scoring errors midway.

See also

create_NICHESObject for the wrapped pipeline that assembles a full NICHESObject; create_Edgelist_Spatial, create_Edgelist_SamplingByType for the edge-list constructors; load_LRM_database for the LR-database loader.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(NICHESv2_inputs)

# Build a spatial kNN edge list (coord must have row names = barcodes)
coord <- data.frame(
  x = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data$x,
  y = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data$y,
  row.names = rownames(NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data)
)
edge.list <- create_Edgelist_Spatial(coord = coord, k = 5L, n.cores = 1L)
#> [create_Edgelist_Spatial] Mode: kNN    | Param: 5 | Cells: 80 | Inter-cell: 274 | Autocrine: 80

# Score every edge x LRM pair (returns a plain 2-element list)
result <- compute_CellToCell(
  count.mtx    = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,
  edge.list    = edge.list,
  LRM.db       = NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db,
  ligand.col   = "ligand",
  receptor.col = "receptor",
  method       = "product",
  n.cores      = 1L
)
#> [compute_CellToCell] 354 edges x 15 LR pairs | method = 'product' | cores = 1
#> [compute_CellToCell] Done. 190 non-zero edge signals.

str(result, max.level = 1)   # $edges and $lr.meta
#> List of 2
#>  $ edges  :Classes ‘data.table’ and 'data.frame':	190 obs. of  10 variables:
#>   ..- attr(*, ".internal.selfref")=<pointer: 0x561c81605a30> 
#>   ..- attr(*, "sorted")= chr [1:3] "from" "to" "LRM"
#>  $ lr.meta:Classes ‘data.table’ and 'data.frame':	15 obs. of  4 variables:
#>   ..- attr(*, ".internal.selfref")=<pointer: 0x561c81605a30> 
#>   ..- attr(*, "sorted")= chr [1:2] "ligand" "receptor"
head(result$edges)           # one row per non-zero (edge, LRM)
#> Key: <from, to, LRM>
#>       from      to     x.from    y.from       x.to      y.to ligand receptor
#>     <char>  <char>      <num>     <num>      <num>     <num> <char>   <char>
#> 1:  Cell_1  Cell_1 0.13612093 0.2979561 0.13612093 0.2979561 Gene11   Gene12
#> 2:  Cell_1  Cell_1 0.13612093 0.2979561 0.13612093 0.2979561  Gene9   Gene10
#> 3: Cell_10  Cell_1 0.08153932 0.2934977 0.13612093 0.2979561  Gene9   Gene10
#> 4: Cell_10 Cell_10 0.08153932 0.2934977 0.08153932 0.2934977 Gene15   Gene16
#> 5: Cell_10  Cell_4 0.08153932 0.2934977 0.03535238 0.2339655  Gene9   Gene10
#> 6: Cell_12 Cell_12 0.23674938 0.4357651 0.23674938 0.4357651 Gene11   Gene12
#>    score           LRM
#>    <num>        <char>
#> 1:    12 Gene11|Gene12
#> 2:    14  Gene9|Gene10
#> 3:    21  Gene9|Gene10
#> 4:    35 Gene15|Gene16
#> 5:    18  Gene9|Gene10
#> 6:    24 Gene11|Gene12
head(result$lr.meta)         # one row per valid LRM pair
#> Key: <ligand, receptor>
#>    ligand receptor  pathway           LRM

#> 1:  Gene1    Gene2 PathwayA   Gene1|Gene2

# Spatial edge lists carry coordinates -- they propagate to $edges
setdiff(c("x.from", "y.from", "x.to", "y.to"), colnames(result$edges))
